When people used to trade, it was because of personal need or to satisfy desire. A goat for a hen. Three eggs for a jumper.

Then along came universal currency, a seemingly brilliant idea designed to simplify trade.

From this sprang capitalism, which reversed the concept of trade completely. Instead of the trade itself being the focus, the acquisition of the new universal currency (i.e. profit) became the focus. Trades began to happen unnecessarily simply to increase profit.

In order to make a profit on an item, a trader must inflate the price. This is important because previously people simply wanted trades to be fair. But with profit as the new goal, people suddenly wanted trades to be less than fair. They wanted trades to be as heavily in favour of themselves as possible, and hence to accumulate as much profit as possible.

So, a situation emerged with capitalism where the price of literally everything sold came to be artificially raised so that someone can make a profit on it. Often, in fact, prices are raised even higher so that a chain of people can respectively make a profit.

If advertisers were honest -- if anyone were honest under capitalism -- they would invite you to buy a deliberately overpriced item which very probably has been constructed in such a way as to break after a set amount of time, forcing you to buy another.
